column1: # The rolling PORT cpu_s baseline (rulings BO / BP4) -- the PREVIOUS TASK's number,
# never the jar's. scripts/quality-ab.sh reads it as the reference for its cpu_s
# column and rewrites it in place at each task's close, in the same commit as
# SEEDING, and why the per-stem numbers are measured rather than copied.
# The plan seeds this file from the v1.0.0-rs run of record's per-board cpu_s. That
# run is the port's measured pre-fix position and is the right provenance -- but its
# 605 boards are the `pcbench` corpus (`pcbench-*`), and this file's 29 rows are the
# `tests/reference/` stems. The two sets are disjoint: not one stem is a pcbench
# board, so there is no per-stem number in that run to copy. The seed is therefore
# Task 0's own median-of-3 measurement of the same binary generation (the branch's
# base commit is what produced v1.0.0-rs), and the run of record is recorded here as
# the corpus-level position every milestone's cpu ratio is taken against.
# v1.0.0-rs corpus cpu_s: cells 605, median 3.040, mean 25.199, total 15245.2
#   (quoted -- benchmark/results/ is gitignored and this checkout has no copy)
# T9 NOTE (ruling BP4): four of these rows are the pre-authorised #227 escalation and
# six more are flagged SLOWER. `router-dac2020-bm01` and `router-strict-drc-cnh` are
# 26x-48x their T8 numbers because the optimizer stage began working; the corpus
# median moved 1.001x. These are the numbers the next task is measured against, and
# they will move again if the controller reworks #227.
